title: A Tiny Spider With More DNA Than You
summary: This spider is only about as big as a quarter and lives its whole life hiding underground. But inside its tiny body, it carries more DNA than a human. The spider is called Aptostichus stephencolberti. It is a trapdoor spider from the sandy dunes of Northern California. Scientists have now read its genome, its complete set of DNA. They found 4.6 billion DNA base pairs, about 50 percent more than the human genome. It also has 52 chromosomes, while human cells have 46. Jason Bond, a teacher at the University of California, Davis, who led the work, said the genome is significant. The results were shared in the Journal of Heredity. Trapdoor spiders are shy hunters that live underground in silk-lined tunnels. Each tunnel has a hinged door. When an insect walks close by, the spider bursts out to catch it. Do not worry if you meet one: its venom is not dangerous to people. The spider's name has a funny story. In 2008, TV host Stephen Colbert learned Bond had named a spider after rock star Neil Young. Colbert asked for one named after him. Bond said yes. Rising seas threaten the dunes where this spider lives.
why_it_matters: Even a tiny spider can hold big surprises in its DNA, and its home needs our care.
